nodes.label: Next.js Pitchdeck Site
nodes.rationale: A single-page, scroll-driven investor pitch site built with Next.js App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Framer Motion.

nodes.label: Strict Black White Red Palette
nodes.rationale: Use only black, white, and red, with no glow, glass, parallax orbs, gradient text, or decorative icons; rely on type, hairline rules, and deck photography.

nodes.label: Centralized Jedlik Content Data
nodes.rationale: All copy and figures live in src/data/jedlikData.ts while section components render the data and hold no copy of their own.

nodes.label: One Component Per Section
nodes.rationale: The layout uses one component per narrative section plus a shared Nav, with assets kept under public/assets.

nodes.label: Framer Motion Scroll Entrances
nodes.rationale: Motion is limited to subtle scroll-driven entrances, market count-ups, and a single funding-timeline bar.

nodes.label: Reduced Motion Final-State Rule
nodes.rationale: prefers-reduced-motion collapses animation to the final state.

nodes.label: Product Withholding Spine
nodes.rationale: Withhold the vehicle as a blacked-out silhouette with a question mark through the positioning, team, and funding beats, tease the unveil on slide 6, and reveal the e-POD on slide 7; the silhouette persists in the header and creates pressure before payoff.

nodes.label: Standalone Pitchdeck Site
nodes.rationale: A new standalone site in the pitchdeck repository cleanly separates the investor experience from the marketing site.

nodes.label: Vite React TypeScript Tailwind Stack
nodes.rationale: Vite, React 18, TypeScript, and Tailwind match the team's existing stack.

nodes.label: GSAP ScrollTrigger and Lenis
nodes.rationale: GSAP ScrollTrigger supplies scroll-driven timelines and Lenis supplies the inertial smooth-scroll feel of the animation reference.

nodes.label: Continuous Scroll Navigation
nodes.rationale: One route and continuous scroll should read as a modern mobile site rather than a deck being swiped.

nodes.label: Light Faithful Palette
nodes.rationale: The deck is light, and the reference demonstrates that the scroll language works on off-white grounds.

nodes.label: Public Investor Ask
nodes.rationale: The ask is public because this is the simplest link to share and is already in the circulated deck.

nodes.label: Crimson #D10A3C
nodes.rationale: Primary accent for headings, key figures, and the wordmark.

nodes.label: Crimson Deep #8E0526
nodes.rationale: Gradient partner for the closing section.

nodes.label: Navy #2B3340
nodes.rationale: Body and secondary-heading type color.

nodes.label: Mist Blue-Grey to Warm-Grey Gradient
nodes.rationale: Soft blue-grey to warm-grey grounding gradient.

nodes.label: Paper White #FFFFFF
nodes.rationale: Cards and panels use paper white.

nodes.label: Lime #B8E62E
nodes.rationale: Sparing accent for the steer-by-wire chip and the phrase move differently.

nodes.label: Ink #111417
nodes.rationale: Used for the question-mark silhouette and photo-grid frames.

nodes.label: Poppins
nodes.rationale: Geometric display capitals matching the deck headings.

nodes.label: DM Sans
nodes.rationale: Body copy typeface.

nodes.label: E-POD Wordmark
nodes.rationale: Heavy italic condensed display treatment set as type so it remains crisp.

nodes.label: Logo Lockup and Tagline
nodes.rationale: Persistent top-left logo lockup with the Redefine the class. tagline.

nodes.label: 2026 Year Marker
nodes.rationale: Persistent top-right year marker.

nodes.label: Question-Mark Vehicle Silhouette
nodes.rationale: Blackout silhouette hides the product before reveal and becomes the progress indicator.

nodes.label: Title Section
nodes.rationale: Opening beat uses a pencil-sketch street scene, SVG stroke-dashoffset drawing, and staggered crimson JEDLIK MOTORS words to introduce the urban-commuting thesis and Ányos Jedlik legacy.

nodes.label: Needs Section
nodes.rationale: Frames the product problem as a better way to move, with eleven urban commuter needs presented as staggered icons and responsive 2-column versus 6+5 layouts.

nodes.label: Positioning Section
nodes.rationale: Maps vehicles by comfort and maneuverability, sequencing competitors before placing Jedlik alone in the high-comfort/high-maneuverability quadrant.

nodes.label: Team Section
nodes.rationale: Builds confidence in the forces behind the unknown product through founders, 15+ years of automotive experience, mentors, and expanding portrait masks; corrects Sertel spelling.

nodes.label: Funding Section
nodes.rationale: Uses a horizontally pinned funding timeline with the NOW ask centered and counting valuations/returns; mobile switches to a scroll-snapped carousel because iOS Safari pinning is unreliable.

nodes.label: Tease Section
nodes.rationale: A blurred vehicle comes into focus while copy announces a new class of vehicle and the imminent unveil.

nodes.label: Reveal Section
nodes.rationale: Full-bleed desert render, E-POD wordmark, and sequential leader-line callouts deliver the product payoff; mobile moves callouts below the render for legibility.

nodes.label: Technology Section
nodes.rationale: Explains the two-wheel vehicle's differentiating steer-by-wire and crab-walk mechanisms with animated inline SVG diagrams that make steering angles tangible.

nodes.label: Market Section
nodes.rationale: Quantifies the 2-wheeler opportunity through a TAM-to-SAM-to-SOM funnel, India statistics, country bars, and count-up/fill animations.

nodes.label: Customers Section
nodes.rationale: Defines three target personas with TAM shares, triggers, decision criteria, acquisition channels, and lifetime value, visualized with donut rings.

nodes.label: Close Section
nodes.rationale: Closes with a crimson-to-deep-crimson flood, a differentiated-mobility message, direct contacts, build-photo grid, and named supporter logos.

nodes.label: Jedlik Positioning
nodes.rationale: The unknown Jedlik vehicle is claimed to occupy the high-comfort/high-maneuverability quadrant alone.

nodes.label: Sertel Naming Correction
nodes.rationale: The team band must say Sertel, correcting the deck's Serte typo.

nodes.label: FY2026 Pre-seed Ask
nodes.rationale: The public NOW ask is ₹7 Cr at ₹75 Cr valuation, with MVP completion, testing and ARAI approval, pilot readiness, and road-legal homologation milestones.

nodes.label: Steer-by-Wire
nodes.rationale: A computer sends the turn command through a wire instead of a rigid steel column, yielding lighter, faster, more precise steering.

nodes.label: Crab-Walk Steering
nodes.rationale: Front and rear wheels turn together so the e-POD can glide sideways for tight, wiggle-free parking.

nodes.label: Global 2-Wheeler TAM
nodes.rationale: TAM is $7.0B per year across 60M two-wheelers sold worldwide.

nodes.label: Enclosed Weatherproof SAM
nodes.rationale: SAM is $1.6B per year for 3.5M enclosed, weatherproof units globally.

nodes.label: Jedlik 2030 SOM
nodes.rationale: SOM target is $70M ARR from 0.8M units across 15 countries by 2030.

nodes.label: India Enclosed e-2W Opportunity
nodes.rationale: India has 230M two-wheelers, 18M annual new sales, 1.08M electric sales in 2024, and a projected $517M enclosed e-2W opportunity by 2030.

nodes.label: Weather Exposed Commuters
nodes.rationale: Primary persona at 60% of TAM: urban salaried adults who currently use open two-wheelers and are triggered by bad monsoon commutes.

nodes.label: Family Buyer
nodes.rationale: Persona at 25% of TAM: family decision-makers seeking step-in access, storage, and brand trust after a child reaches 12–14 or a second child arrives.

nodes.label: Premium Aspirant
nodes.rationale: Persona at 15% of TAM: tech-savvy premium-metro buyers comparing a small car or premium two-wheeler and responding to a grand launch or wow test ride.

nodes.label: Market Expansion Regions
nodes.rationale: Next markets are India $517M, Vietnam and Thailand $86M, Indonesia $63M, EU-5 and USA $40M+, and Brazil $8M.

nodes.label: Typed Section Data Architecture
nodes.rationale: Typed exports in src/data keep figures, names, and labels auditable; sections describe content while reusable motion primitives describe animation wiring.

nodes.label: Progress Rail
nodes.rationale: Shared component renders the question-mark silhouette and beat markers and therefore knows the whole sequence.

nodes.label: One Lenis Instance
nodes.rationale: useLenis creates one smooth-scroll instance that drives ScrollTrigger.update for every ScrollTrigger.

nodes.label: Sticky Over Pin
nodes.rationale: Long scroll containers with position: sticky children avoid transform jitter from ScrollTrigger.pin on iOS Safari.

nodes.label: Reduced-Motion Static Readability
nodes.rationale: Reduced motion resolves entrances immediately, makes scrubbed sequences static, stops wheel loops, and leaves the page fully readable without motion.

nodes.label: Animation Trigger Visibility Rule
nodes.rationale: Nothing may remain hidden without a reveal trigger; failed triggers must not make content permanently invisible.

nodes.label: Mobile LCP Budget
nodes.rationale: Target under 2.5s LCP on a 4G phone with no hero layout shift, optimized responsive assets, lazy loading, limited dependencies, and below-fold code splitting.

nodes.label: Market Citation Gap
nodes.rationale: SIAM 2024 is cited for the 18M figure, while other market and valuation numbers lack citations; a Sources note is recommended before circulation.

nodes.label: Forward-Looking Valuation Targets
nodes.rationale: Valuations and return multiples up to 357.9x are projections presented as targets, not commitments.

nodes.label: Sources Footer Note
nodes.rationale: A footer sources note should be added before the public link is circulated.
